text: October 17, 2026

name: TextBox 13
text: Simple decisions for Stories

name: TextBox 14
text: Hours, stock, waste, prices and offers, explained simply

name: TextBox 15
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

Stories Coffee operational recommendations. Evidence: local transaction data for January–June 2026. Numerical examples explicitly marked as illustrative. MSFEA typography, logos and layouts reused from the existing project deck.

title: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

text: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

name: TextBox 11
text: Opening hours: test a later start

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Keep the busy evening hours

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: Uptown’s 7 AM hour earns just $4.37 after product costs. Open later only if the staff and energy savings cover lost sales.

name: TextBox 18
text: Uptown’s 7 AM gross profit per calendar day

name: TextBox 20
text: 9 PM baskets across all branches, Jan–Jun

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Check removable staff hours. Test Uptown at 9 AM and Garden at 8 AM.
Check  Restore hours if full-day earnings after operating costs fall.

Observed: reports/tables/outside_hour_economics.csv and reports/tables/hour.csv. 181 calendar days, January–June 2026. Early-hour labor and energy costs are unmeasured. Opening at 09:00/08:00 is a pilot candidate, not a proven optimum. Compare matched days and track whether early buyers return later. Gross profit means net revenue minus recorded product cost, before labor and rent.

name: TextBox 11
text: Branch closing: check the full bill

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Fewer sales alone do not justify closing a branch

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: Uptown is the smallest branch, but still earns money before rent and wages. Check costs we can actually remove before closing it.

name: TextBox 18
text: Uptown’s daily gross profit, before rent and wages

name: TextBox 19
text: Unknown

name: TextBox 20
text: Rent, payroll savings and exit costs are missing

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Compare avoidable bills plus profit from customers moving to other branches.
Check  Keep the branch if savings do not cover lost profit and exit costs.

Source: reports/tables/branches.csv. Uptown gross profit $34,882.06 / 181 = $192.72 per calendar day. Permanent closure gain = avoidable operating costs + recaptured contribution at other branches - lost branch contribution - exit costs. Capacity, migration, contractual costs, and actual avoidable bills are unknown. Garden costs should also be reconciled to invoices before evaluating profitability. No branch closure is established by these data.

name: TextBox 11
text: Restocking: buy for the next delivery

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Start with Iced Latte, Iced Matcha and Butter Croissant

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: These are the three best-selling products by units. Plan each branch separately. Buy enough until the next delivery, plus a small buffer.

name: TextBox 17
text: 20/day

name: TextBox 18
text: Example only: expected sales of one item

name: TextBox 19
text: 35 units

name: TextBox 20
text: 2 days × 20 + 5 buffer − 10 usable in stock

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Use recent same-weekday sales. Subtract usable stock and confirmed deliveries.
Check  Reduce the buffer if leftovers rise. Increase it if true stockouts recur.

Source: stories_transactions.csv, quantities summed by product. Iced Latte 2,629, Iced Matcha 2,322, Butter Croissant 2,238 units in January–June 2026. The 35-unit example is illustrative, not a computed order recommendation. For ingredients, convert product forecasts using verified recipes and supplier pack sizes. Stock, supplier lead time, shelf life, inventory positions and lost demand are absent. Exclude expired stock and avoid ordering more than can sell before expiry.

title: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

name: TextBox 11
text: Waste: make smaller batches first

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Discount only safe food that is likely to be left over

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: Log what gets thrown away and why. Prepare pastries in smaller batches. Mark down surplus close to its safe selling deadline.

name: TextBox 17
text: 5 left

name: TextBox 18
text: Example only: five pastries would otherwise be discarded

name: TextBox 20
text: Five genuinely extra sales at $3.06 each

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Test a 20% markdown on surplus Harbour Butter Croissants, normally $3.83.
Check  End the offer if lost full-price sales and handling cost exceed money recovered.

Price source: stories_transactions.csv, Harbour Butter Croissant unit price $3.83, recorded unit cost $1.14. Illustrative markdown price rounded to $3.06. Five otherwise discarded units sold bring $15.30 incremental receipts, before extra handling, substitution and disposal effects. Already produced cost is sunk for the sell-versus-discard decision, but must be included in future batch planning. No actual waste or expiry records exist. Confirm food safety and shelf life. Track prepared/sold/discarded units, reason and stockout times.

text: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

name: TextBox 11
text: Price increase: try a small step

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Check supplier invoices, then test one item

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: A small price rise can help if customers keep buying. Start with Iced Latte at one branch and watch the whole basket, not just that drink.

name: TextBox 18
text: Recorded Harbour Iced Latte list price

name: TextBox 20
text: Example test price, about 5% higher

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Test against comparable unchanged periods. Track visitors, baskets and complaints.
Check  Roll back if earnings after costs fall or customers shift away.

Source: stories_transactions.csv. Harbour Iced Latte list price $5.62, recorded unit cost $1.66, fixed throughout the extract. $5.90 is an illustrative rounded +5% test price, not an estimated optimal price. Elasticity is unknown. Refresh actual costs first, especially Garden’s roughly 43% same-item cost difference. Prefer randomized stable eligibility or comparable service blocks if feasible. Track whole-basket contribution, nonbuyers, substitutions and purchases moving among branches. Do not combine with combo or discount experiments.

title: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

name: TextBox 11
text: Price decrease: earn back the cut

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: A lower price must bring enough extra purchases

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: A 10% croissant price cut leaves less money per sale. It pays only if extra sales cover the discount and any extra work or waste.

name: TextBox 18
text: Harbour Butter Croissant gross profit at $3.83

name: TextBox 20
text: Approximate extra units needed at $3.45 to break even

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Test a temporary cut on one item and compare total basket earnings.
Check  Keep the normal price if extra profit does not cover the price cut.

Source: stories_transactions.csv. Harbour Butter Croissant price $3.83, recorded unit cost $1.14. Illustrative lower price $3.45, about 10% off. GP per unit declines from $2.69 to $2.31. Required volume factor = 2.69/2.31 = 1.1645, or 16.45% extra units, rounded conservatively to +17%. Assumes no existing discounts, unchanged cost/mix, no substitution, no extra costs or basket effects. This is a screening calculation, not a demand forecast. Slow sales alone do not show price is the cause.

title: ⓒ All rights reserved. American University of Beirut 2026.

name: TextBox 11
text: Combo offers: start with coffee + bakery

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Two specific pairings to test

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: Try Iced Latte + Butter Croissant first. A second candidate is Iced Matcha + Chocolate Cookie. Suggest the pairing at full price before cutting it.

name: TextBox 18
text: Harbour Latte + Butter Croissant at list prices

name: TextBox 20
text: Illustrative 10% combo price, if a rebate is needed

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Choose available items with positive margin and quick preparation.
Check  Drop a pair if it replaces better sales, increases waste or slows service.

Sources: stories_transactions.csv and reports/tables/category_pair_null.csv. Harbour Iced Latte $5.62 + Butter Croissant $3.83 = $9.45. Recorded costs $1.66 + $1.14 = $2.80. Illustrative 10% off rounded to $8.51. Bakery + Cold Coffee co-purchase enrichment 1.18× in Jan–Apr and 1.23× in May–Jun after context/basket-size adjustment. Bakery + Matcha & Tea enrichment about 1.76×/1.72×. These support category-level candidates only. The named product pairs are proposals, not established product-level winners. Pairing is association and does not prove an offer causes purchases.

name: TextBox 11
text: How to know which combo pays

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: Count new add-ons and discounts on pairs already selling

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: Check baskets for a drink without a pastry. Test the offer against no offer. Extra add-on profit must pay for rebates on existing pairs.

name: TextBox 18
text: Extra gross profit when a Latte-only buyer adds the $8.51 combo

name: TextBox 19
text: 54 new

name: TextBox 20
text: Add-ons needed per 100 existing pairs, before extra costs

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Rank pairs by extra earnings after rebates, waste and service costs.
Check  Reject an offer if total earnings are lower, even when basket size rises.

Illustrative Harbour Latte/Croissant calculation using supplied list prices and recorded costs. Latte alone GP = 5.62 - 1.66 = 3.96. Combo GP = 8.51 - 2.80 = 5.71. Increment = $1.75 for a new attachment. Each existing full-price pair loses 9.45 - 8.51 = $0.94. One hundred existing pairs lose $94, requiring ceil(94/1.75) = 54 new attachments before program costs, waste, substitutions, lost baskets and existing discounts. This is a screening example, not observed uptake. Analyze actual net prices and match branch/daypart. Randomize offer/no-offer blocks and include all arrivals/completions. Repeat in later weeks before scaling.

name: TextBox 11
text: Discounts: test them in quiet hours

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: A busy shop can lose money by discounting existing demand

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: At Harbour, compare no offer with 10% and 15% morning offers. Count everyone offered the deal, including people who buy nothing.

name: TextBox 17
text: 3 groups

name: TextBox 18
text: No discount, 10% off and 15% off

name: TextBox 19
text: Profit

name: TextBox 20
text: Choose the offer that leaves more money after costs

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Assign offers before purchase in comparable morning periods. Cap the budget.
Check  Pause if earnings per visitor fall or the offer shifts existing sales.

Sources: analysis/outputs/REPORT.md and reports/experiment_plan.md. Prior campaign comparisons are inconclusive and discounted baskets are selected/mechanically larger. Neither 10% nor 15% has proven incremental contribution. Morning is a candidate based on recorded hourly demand, not proven demand elasticity. Use a prespecified test duration/sample size, stable pre-purchase assignment, visitor and nonbuyer logging, comparable weekday/daypart groups, and follow-up. Include discount/program costs, purchases moving between times or branches, queue harm, and whole-chain contribution. January and February are lower in this six-month extract, but annual winter seasonality cannot be established.

name: TextBox 11
text: Start small and keep what pays

name: TextBox 12
text: EECE 490 · Stories Coffee Hackathon

name: TextBox 12
text: One change at a time, with a clear comparison

name: TextBox 15
text: In plain words

name: TextBox 16
text: First record stock, waste, staff hours and real costs. Then test one change in one branch. Expand only when more money stays in the business.

name: TextBox 17
text: Measure

name: TextBox 18
text: Sales minus product, staff, energy, waste and offer costs

name: TextBox 19
text: Compare

name: TextBox 20
text: Similar days with and without the change

name: TextBox 22
text:
Try this  Start with stock and waste logs. Then test hours, one price or one offer.
Check  Pause for lower earnings, longer waits or worse customer experience.

Evidence scope: January 1–June 30, 2026, 181 calendar days, three branches. Sources: reports/recommendations_guide.md, reports/causal_decisions.md and reports/experiment_plan.md. No operational pilot has been performed. Prices, inventory examples and offer uptake on these slides are either observed inputs or explicitly illustrative calculations. Do not add overlapping scenario gains. Gross profit in source tables excludes payroll/rent, so actual operating earnings require new cost records. Missing stock/waste and nonbuyer data constrain decisions. Keep changes separate to identify their effects.
